items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VIII, List of Answers on Topics 57:1
items.html: The Rosh of Aba ve Ima clothes AA from the Peh downward, down to the chest of AA. For the screen of phase two, over which the level of MA of Aba ve Ima came out, is the aspect of the screen of the Guf of phase three, which is the level of AA — just as in the cascading of the Partzufim of AK and Nekudim. Hence, after the inclusion of the coupling of Aba ve Ima in the Rosh of AA was completed, they went out and descended to their place, and came to the place of the chest of AA, and the ten Sefirot of the Rosh came out from the chest upward to the Peh of AA, and the ten Sefirot of the Guf, from the chest downward to the Tabur of AA. And the reason Aba ve Ima were not drawn down to the end of the legs of AA, but were cut off at the Tabur of AA, stems from the power of the correction of the Parsa within the innards of AK, which separates between AB and SAG of AK, considered Akudim, and ZON of AK, considered Nekudim. And so it is also in Atzilut, where the Parsa was corrected within the innards of AA, separating between Aba ve Ima, which are the aspect of Yod-Hey of Atzilut, and ZON, which are the aspect of Vav-Hey of Atzilut. And the difference between them is similar to the difference of the Parsa in AK, for Aba ve Ima, who are above the Parsa, resemble Akudim of AK, meaning that from their root in AK they are clean of the bottom Hey. And ZON, who are below the Parsa of AA, have within them the joining of the bottom Hey with the first Hey even from their root in AK. This will be explained at length in the coming parts.
